segments.text: Thanks for being here. Progress check on opening the second restaurant, on rue des Tanneurs: the lease is signed, three thousand eight hundred euros a month, and we open in five weeks. We'll go through the kitchen, hiring, admin and communication.
The kitchen is ninety percent delivered. The cold room is in place, the only thing missing is the combi oven, which arrives on Thursday. It's the same ten-tray model as at the first restaurant.
On the budget side, we've spent a hundred and twelve thousand euros of the hundred and thirty planned for the works. That leaves eighteen thousand euros of headroom, no more.
The dining room was painted yesterday, only the shop sign on the façade is left, and the maker installs it next week.
Karim, when the oven arrives, can you run the full test with the technician? I want a steam test and a convection test before we sign for the delivery.
Yes, I'll handle it. I'll run the test on Monday with the technician, steam and convection.
And the menu, where are we? The menu printer is waiting for the text.
I'll send you the final menu by Friday: six starters, eight mains and five desserts.
Great. For the wines, Karim told me last night: “I'll prepare the food and wine pairings for you for next week.” So we're waiting for that before ordering from the wine merchant.
OK. Another topic, opening days. I propose we close on Mondays, like at the first restaurant.
Yes, closed on Mondays, it keeps the rotas simple.
Fine with me too, Monday it is.
Monday works for me.
Perfect, it's decided: the new restaurant will be closed on Mondays. Sophie, on the admin side?

The licence application has to be filed with the town hall. On the portal, the deadline shown is 2026-11-10. I'll file it by that date at the latest. The safety inspection will then be scheduled by the town hall after filing.
Very good. The new premises will also have to be declared to the insurer before opening, otherwise the work on the extractor hood isn't covered.
On hiring, we need three waiters and a dishwasher. Right now, a waiter ad gets about ten applications a week. I'll write the job ads and post them by Wednesday.
I also need two kitchen assistants. And all the new hires will have to take the food hygiene training: I'll take care of registering them.
For the till, I propose we keep the same software as in the first restaurant, so the figures are comparable. Do you agree?
Yes, same software, that works for me.
Agreed as well.
That said, I'm keeping my own spreadsheet for the bank reconciliations. That's just how I work.
Noted. So that's settled: the same till software in both restaurants. Sophie, for the terrace, can you ask for three furniture quotes? Tables and chairs for twenty covers.
Yes, I'll ask for the three quotes this week.
On communication, I'll create the restaurant's Instagram account and post the first photos of the works by Friday.
And the photos of the dishes for the website?
I might be able to take them during the kitchen trials, if I have a moment. No guarantees.
Careful, the plating won't be final until the kitchen trials are over.
Karim, could you organize a tasting for the local press before opening?
That one I won't promise. A tasting without a full kitchen team is risky. Let's talk about suppliers instead.
Good segue. Has the fishmonger replied?
Yes. The fishmonger from Pornic agrees to deliver to both restaurants three times a week, with a five percent volume discount.
Five percent, on our volumes, comes to roughly four hundred euros a month.
Another idea: a loyalty card shared by both restaurants?
It's a good idea, but we'll keep it for after the opening. We'll come back to it in January.
And the VAT return for the new business, who's handling it?
Gilles, our accountant, will do it. He isn't here today.
Back to the menu. I'm correcting what I said: on Friday you'll only get a provisional version, without the desserts. The final menu will wait until the kitchen trials are over.
By the way, we can skip the combi oven test, right? The supplier told me the oven is factory-tested before shipping.
No, I'm keeping it. The factory test says nothing about our installation. I'm running the test on Monday as planned.
OK. As for the job ads, though, I won't manage with everything else. Sophie, can you take them over?
Yes, I'll take them over. I'll post them on Friday on the two job sites.
And for the wines, I confirm what Thomas said: I'm preparing the food and wine pairings, you'll have them on Tuesday.
Thanks. Sophie, about the terrace furniture quotes, I'm cancelling my request: the landlord is leaving us his tables and chairs.
Perfect, that frees up some time.
Karim, what if Sophie also took over the hygiene training registrations? It's mostly paperwork.
Not this week, I'm tied up with the licence and the ads. I can't take them on.
I also need to go back on Instagram: I'm withdrawing my commitment, I won't create the account. With my shifts at the first restaurant, I won't have time to run it.

One last point from me, the closing day. I looked at the first restaurant's figures: Monday lunch is our best service of the week, eighty-five covers on average against forty on Tuesdays. I suggest we go back on closing on Mondays and close on Tuesdays instead.
It changes the rotas, but the figures are clear. Tuesday is fine with me.
Same for me, even though Tuesday was our fish delivery day.
Then we're reversing the earlier decision: the new restaurant will open on Mondays and close on Tuesdays. Who can call the fishmonger to fit the deliveries around this change?
Nobody? All right, I'll call him myself tomorrow morning.
Thanks, everyone, we'll check in again in a week.
